 Live .  5,453 viewing 5453 viewing Live page Updated 11 minutes ago Meghan's father Thomas Markle due in court after arrest on charge relating to child sex abuse material
 Summary
 Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been charged over the possession of child sex abuse material 
 He is due to appear in court in Tampa, Florida, later at about 18:30 GMT (13:30 ET)
 Markle was arrested after the FBI searched two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for almost 20 years - here's more from the Department of Justice statement 
 Images published by news outlets alongside reports of the 82-year-old's arrest appear to show him in handcuffs surrounded by FBI personnel 
 Markle has previously denied allegations of possessing images of child sex abuse, calling the claims "sick lies"
 The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018 - in a statement last month , the wife of Prince Harry said: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed"
 She added that she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father
 Media caption, Watch: The BBC's Ione Wells explains the charges facing Thomas Markle Live Reporting
 Edited by Kieran Kelly and Manish Pandey
 Thomas Markle due in court after arrest on charge relating to child sex abuse material - recap published at 18:05 GMT 18:05 GMT 
 Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is due to appear in a Florida court after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material. 
 The US Department of Justice (DoJ) earlier confirmed the 82-year-old had been arrested and "charged with one count of possession of child pornography ". 
 The department said he was arrested on a federal criminal complaint alleging he kept child sex abuse material, "including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades".
 FBI director Kash Patel said authorities "moved quickly, identified and located the explicit material" and arrested Markle in Florida - more on his statement here . 
 Markle has previously strongly denied the allegations that he had possessed images of child abuse, labelling them as "sick lies".
 The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are so far not commenting on the arrest of Meghan's father. Last month Meghan confirmed that in 2019 she had been forwarded a letter by the UK's Metropolitan Police making “disturbing allegations” about Thomas Markle .
 Markle Sr is due to make his initial appearance in the United States District Court in the Middle District of Florida in Tampa at 13:30 ET (18:30 GMT).

 There will be no cameras when Thomas Markle appears in court published at 17:36 GMT 17:36 GMT 
 Ione Wells 
North America correspondent 
 Image source, AP Image caption, Markle will appear at the United States District Court in the Middle District of Florida
 In about an hour , Thomas Markle Sr will make his first court appearance at a district court in Florida.
 There are no cameras allowed inside the courtroom.
 It’s not clear how much detail we will get from this appearance, but we may learn whether he plans to plead guilty or not guilty to the charge, and whether he will remain in custody or could be released on bail.

 What does it mean for a case to be under seal? published at 17:15 GMT 17:15 GMT 
 Earlier, when news of Thomas Markle's arrest first emerged, we were told that the case was under seal .
 Being under seal may mean not all details of a case are made public. 
 Sealing a case is often done to protect victim identities or keep confidential information private. 
 The judge can always choose to unseal the indictment if they believe the public interest outweighs those privacy concerns.

 Markle to appear in court today published at 16:52 GMT 16:52 GMT 
 Thomas Markle is due to make his initial appearance in court at 13:30 ET (18:30 GMT) today.
 It will take place at the United States District Court in the Middle District of Florida in Tampa, the DoJ earlier said.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 No comment from Duke and Duchess of Sussex published at 16:40 GMT 16:40 GMT 
 Sean Coughlan 
Royal correspondent 
 Image source, PA Media The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are so far not commenting on the arrest of Meghan’s father, according to a spokesman for the couple.
 But on Tuesday, Prince Harry and Meghan are due to appear in Brussels, opening the so-called Lost Screen Memorial, which remembers children who lost their lives because of the harms of social media. That’s likely to include a speech about keeping children safe online. 
 They may well be asked questions about Thomas Markle and the situation in Meghan’s family in the US.
 Last month Meghan confirmed that in 2019 she had been forwarded a letter by the UK's Metropolitan Police making “disturbing allegations” about Thomas Markle. The letter had been written by his first wife.

 Markle 'allegedly targeted innocent children', says FBI director published at 16:30 GMT 16:30 GMT 
 FBI director Kash Patel says authorities "moved quickly" in the arrest of Thomas Markle. 
 In a statement, Patel says: "Mr. Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions."
 FBI agents worked with the US Department of Justice and "moved quickly, identified and located the explicit material, and arrested Mr. Markle in Florida", he says. 
 Patel adds: "This FBI will use every single resource at our disposal to protect innocent kids – any predator who targets children will have zero safe haven in this country or anywhere they try to hide."

 Markle due to appear in court in Florida on Friday published at 16:14 GMT 16:14 GMT 
 We can now bring you more from the statement released just now by the US Department of Justice.
 Thomas Markle, the statement says, has been "charged with one count of possession of child pornography". 
 The statement alleges Markle "kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades". 
 Giving detail about the searches leading to Markle's arrest, the statement describes searches of Los Angeles storage units rented by Markle since 2008. 
 Inside, it says, "agents seized approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives, and books that contained suspected CSAM (child sexual abuse material)".
 Markle is expected to appear later today in United States District Court in the Middle District of Florida in Tampa, the statement adds.
 Image source, ITV/Shutterstock

 US Department of Justice says Markle has been charged published at 16:08 GMT 16:08 GMT Breaking 
 The US Department of Justice says: "A Florida man was arrested today on a federal criminal complaint alleging he kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades.
 "Thomas Wayne Markle, 82, of Lakeland, Florida, is charged with one count of possession of child pornography."

 CBS: Thomas Markle was arrested in Florida published at 15:57 GMT 15:57 GMT 
 Thomas Markle was arrested in Florida, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS News.
 Pictures published by the Daily Mail and the Sun appear to show Markle in handcuffs surrounded by FBI personnel while he sits in a wheelchair.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Meghan said she was 'deeply distressed' over allegations against her father published at 15:48 GMT 15:48 GMT 
 In a statement released last month after the allegations about her father emerged, the Duchess of Sussex said in a statement: "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."
 She added that she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father.

 What we know, and don't know, about Thomas Markle Sr's arrest published at 15:35 GMT 15:35 GMT 
 What we know: 
 Thomas Markle Sr - the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex - has been arrested in connection with allegations he possessed child sex abuse material, according to the BBC’s US partner CBS News
 Markle has strongly denied all allegations against him previously, and labelled recent allegations that he had possessed images of child abuse as "sick lies"
 His daughter Meghan revealed in October that she had been informed by letter about “disturbing allegations” in early 2019
 What we don’t know: 
 When Markle Sr was arrested - and where
 Whether the Duchess of Sussex has been informed

 Sources say 82-year-old arrested over allegations he possessed child sex abuse material published at 15:25 GMT 15:25 GMT 
 Three sources familiar with the matter tell CBS News - the BBC's US media partner - Meghan's father Thomas Markle has been arrested in connection with allegations he possessed child sex abuse material. 
 The case remains under seal, one of the sources adds.

 Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been arrested over allegations he possessed child sex abuse material.
 This is a breaking news story - we'll bring you more information shortly
